The increasing width of the confidence intervals across the different horizons reflects the compounding nature of uncertainty. Conversely, a major breakthrough in technology, unexpectedly robust economic growth, a swift resolution to existing global tensions, or a surprisingly positive earnings report could trigger a substantial rally, pushing the asset above the upper bound of the forecast. These types of low-probability, high-impact events, often termed "black swans," are inherently difficult to quantify but represent the primary risk to any probabilistic forecast.
